children: Australian Finance Group keeps its bull at Macquarie despite a September-quarter decline in mortgage lodgements. With interest rates rising and housing markets slowing, AFG's network mortgage lodgements fell 12% over the three months through September. However, a note from one of Macquarie's analysts points out that AFG's securitization loan book grew from A$7.1 billion to A$7.3 billion despite reduced activity. The note adds that AFG's market share improved in August and September, which should support future relative performance. Macquarie keeps an outperform rating on the stock and trims its target price 7.2% to 2.18 Australian dollars. Shares are at A$1.25 ahead of the open. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
